keyRules: In the Open Category the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point of the ground surface — not simply straight down, so when flying near a slope, the adjacent ground may also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (taller than 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or could transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy in a collision) — this applies even to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.
The registration number must be visible on the drone and (for C1–C3 class drones) entered into the Remote ID system

Drones without a C class mark (placed on the market before 2024-01-01) and privately built drones may fly only in the A1 subcategory if their take-off mass is less than 250 g, or in the A3 subcategory if less than 25 kg

The minimum age for a remote pilot is 16 (EU rule; Lithuania has not lowered it). Younger pilots may fly only: under the direct supervision of a remote pilot who meets the requirements; with a C0 class toy in the A1 subcategory; or with a privately built drone with a take-off mass of less than 250 g. The A1/A3 training and exam are completed in the TKA system, and the certificate is valid for 5 years.
Civil liability insurance is mandatory for drones weighing more than 20 kg

In the Open Category you must keep the drone within your own direct, unaided visual line of sight (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen don't count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication with each other at all times so that together you can scan the airspace and avoid collisions. “Follow-me” mode is a separate exception, allowed up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

There is no single EU-wide distance from airports that you must keep. Restrictions near airports are published as geographical zones (Article 15), whose shape and size vary from airport to airport – before flying near an airport, aerodrome or heliport, check the official drone zone map. In controlled airspace (Vilnius, Kaunas, Palanga, Šiauliai UR zones) you may fly in the Open Category without prior authorisation only up to the height set for the zone – the closer to the airport, the lower (heights – utm.ans.lt; flying higher requires an authorisation issued under the LTSA procedure). In aerodrome ATZ/TIZ zones the flight must be coordinated in advance with the aerodrome owner or operator.
Flights in EYP zones and over military areas (EYURM) are prohibited without authorisation; the same applies in activated EYR zones (activation is announced by NOTAM)
Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline when the required green flashing light is used, unless a current geographic zone or national rule imposes a stricter condition.
Restrictions are in effect in the Curonian Spit National Park
In the border zone along the borders with Belarus and Russia (about 7.4 km from the border), flights without prior coordination are strictly prohibited
importantNotes: Registration and issuing/renewing the registration certificate costs 31 €
Insurance is required only for drones weighing more than 20 kg
In the border zone along the borders with Belarus and Russia (about 7.4 km from the border), flights without prior coordination are strictly prohibited
The Vilnius Airport CTR covers a large part of the city
The GDPR applies when identifiable individuals are filmed or photographed
